rubrics.criterion: The merged workspace-resource capability contract is gone from the v2 SDK resource API layer: no class in that layer aggregates abstract capability obligations from two or more operation-family interfaces without implementing them and pushes them onto descendant resource classes (the umbrella contract and the per-category profile layers no longer exist as bases of any resource API).
rubrics.rationale: This is the presence condition of the injected relation: the tying of four operation families to every subscriber was created by that single merging-class layer, so its absence is the first-order outcome of the requested rework.

rubrics.criterion: After the rework, every workspace resource API class depends only on the operation families it genuinely serves: for no class does an inherited or declared capability obligation resolve to a body that performs no workspace request (no transport verb call and no workspace-client delegation) while another resource API serves the same family with a real request.
rubrics.rationale: This is the instance's credited smell relation: obligations satisfied by empty-object, empty-list, empty-stream or refusal bodies are exactly the 'silently fake' capabilities the task prompt reports.

rubrics.criterion: The pure configuration resources (secret storage, ingress definitions, templates, ray clusters, dedicated node groups) no longer depend on any of the workload capability families: their classes carry no readiness/termination, replica, log-stream, event-history, stop/restart or fine-tune model-catalog obligations, neither inherited through any contract nor defined as placeholder methods on the resources themselves.
rubrics.rationale: These five resources had the entire merged surface placated at the category-profile level; the task explicitly calls out that configuration resources show empty capability dashboards, so their full decoupling is an observable, independently checkable fact of the fix.

rubrics.criterion: The two batch workload APIs (the job API and the fine-tune API) no longer carry the placeholder capability bodies that existed only to satisfy the merged contract (empty readiness/termination views, empty replica/event/log bodies, lifecycle refusal scaffolding), while their genuinely request-backed families (job log-streaming, replica and event routes; the fine-tune supported-model and trainer catalog routes) remain fully implemented.
rubrics.rationale: Batch resources are where the report's correctness symptom lives (a failing job rendering 'nothing to report'); the fix must both remove the fake views and keep the real request-backed surface intact.

rubrics.criterion: The two pod-path implementations (the legacy pod API and its flag-on devpod counterpart) no longer define the empty replica-list and event-history methods introduced to satisfy the merged contract; a surface that has no replica or event route offers no such method rather than exposing silently-empty ones.
rubrics.rationale: This verifies the mode-switched pair was reconciled rather than half-fixed: both sides of the pair carried matching empty placations, so a solver that only reworks one side leaves part of the reported symptom in place.

rubrics.criterion: Any capability declarations retained in the resource API layer are focused: each declared contract carries the obligations of exactly one operation family, with no contract remaining that mixes families even partially.
rubrics.rationale: Accepts sound refactorings that keep a shared capability vocabulary (so generic tooling can branch on families) but checks that the segregation principle, not just a smaller merge, is what survived; a wholesale removal of contracts also satisfies this item vacuously.

rubrics.criterion: The inheritance wiring of every affected resource API class was updated together with the contract change: each class derives from the shared transport base plus at most the focused capability declarations it genuinely serves, and no resource class still inherits from an intermediate category/umbrella/profile base.
rubrics.rationale: The obligations were propagated through base-class edits in eleven resource modules; removing only the contract definitions without rewiring the subscribers would leave dangling bases or unchanged forced dependencies.

rubrics.criterion: All references to any removed or relocated contract layer were reconciled: the leptonai.api.v2 package contains no dangling import of, inheritance from, or runtime reference to a deleted declaration (no class was left importing symbols that no longer exist).
rubrics.rationale: A wholesale contract removal spans module boundaries; broken imports would turn a correct-looking design change into a non-working tree, and this fact is answerable directly from the patched repository.

rubrics.criterion: The declarations that existed only to host the merged surface were removed outright rather than disabled or hidden: no dead umbrella/profile/aggregation class remains in the layer (not renamed, not superseded by an equally-placating duplicate) and any module left with no remaining purpose does not retain orphaned capability scaffolding.
rubrics.rationale: Obsolete injected artifacts are a required cleanup dimension: leaving the dead merged layers behind keeps the misleading type surface discoverable and invites reintroduction.

rubrics.criterion: Imports that existed only to support the removed placeholder bodies or the removed contract layers were deleted from the resource API modules (for example model/response types that no remaining method in the module uses).
rubrics.rationale: The placeholder bodies dragged workload and catalog model types into modules that never used them before; unused residue of the injection is exactly what this cleanup dimension targets.

rubrics.criterion: The genuinely request-backed capability methods were not damaged by the cleanup: the workload health/termination detail calls, replica listings, live log streams, event history queries, stop/restart requests on the fully capable resources, the job log/replica/event requests and the fine-tune model/trainer catalog requests still issue the same requests with the same routes, parameters and response parsing as before the rework.
rubrics.rationale: The most plausible over-deletion failure for this instance is removing a real method along with the adjacent fake ones; this item is checkable per family against the pre-patch behavior.

rubrics.criterion: The pre-existing, documented unsupported-operation degradations were not silenced or deleted: sub-operations that already degraded with explicit 'not supported by the new API' errors on the flag-on resource surfaces (readiness/termination/live-log detail where no route exists) still raise their explicit errors with the same meaning, and were not converted into silent empty results.
rubrics.rationale: The task explicitly requires deliberate refusals to stay deliberate and visible; turning an honest error into an empty-success view reinstates the exact 'silence masquerading as support' failure the fix is meant to eliminate.

rubrics.criterion: No resource API class was left declaring capability obligations it does not implement: every class in the resource API layer that the workspace client registers is instantiable, so client construction and every resource attribute on the workspace client keep working exactly as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: Removing a contract without completing the rewiring produces abstract-obligation TypeErrors at client construction - the specific construction-path breakage forced by this layer's registration design.

rubrics.criterion: The placation style was not relocated: no replacement shared layer (thinner base class, convenience mixin, or module of default bodies) was created to keep supplying non-requesting bodies for the families the resources cannot serve.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible incomplete repair renames or narrows the profile layer instead of removing it; the task requires capability truth at each resource, not a smaller intermediary that still fakes support.
